DSA.title: Two Pointers
DSA.summary: Use two indices moving toward each other or in the same direction. Eliminates the need for nested loops on sorted data.

DSA.title: Sliding Window
DSA.summary: Maintain a window of elements and expand/shrink as you traverse. Avoids recomputing overlapping subproblems.

DSA.title: Binary Search
DSA.when: Sorted arrays, search space reduction, min/max problems
DSA.summary: Halve the search space each iteration. Can be applied on the answer space, not just arrays.

DSA.title: BFS
DSA.when: Shortest path, level order traversal, graph exploration
DSA.summary: Uses a queue. Explores nodes level by level. Always finds shortest path in unweighted graphs.

DSA.title: DFS
DSA.when: Connected components, cycle detection, topological sort
DSA.summary: Uses recursion or stack. Goes deep before backtracking. Good for exhaustive search.

DSA.title: Dynamic Programming
DSA.summary: Break problem into subproblems, store results to avoid recomputation. Think: can I define this recursively? Can I cache?

DSA.title: Backtracking
DSA.summary: Build candidates incrementally and abandon ('backtrack') as soon as a candidate cannot lead to a valid solution.

DSA.title: Heap / Priority Queue
DSA.summary: Use a min-heap for smallest-first, max-heap for largest-first. Python's heapq is min by default; negate values for max.

DSA.title: Union-Find
DSA.when: Connected components, cycle detection in undirected graphs
DSA.summary: Track component membership with path compression and union by rank. Near-constant time per operation at scale.

DSA.title: Trie
DSA.complexity: O(m) insert/search where m = word length
DSA.summary: Tree where each node is a character. Efficient for prefix-based lookups that hash maps can't handle naturally.

DSA.title: Monotonic Stack
DSA.summary: Stack where elements are always increasing or decreasing. Pop when the invariant would be violated — that pop is your answer.

DSA.title: Fast & Slow Pointers
DSA.when: Cycle detection in linked lists, finding middle node
DSA.summary: Slow moves one step, fast moves two. They meet inside a cycle. If fast reaches null, there is no cycle.

System Design.title: Load Balancer
System Design.summary: Routes requests to servers using algorithms like round robin, least connections, or IP hash. Prevents any single server from being overwhelmed.

System Design.title: Caching
System Design.summary: Store frequently accessed data in fast storage (Redis, Memcached). Consider: cache-aside, write-through, write-behind. Always think about invalidation.

System Design.title: Database Sharding
System Design.summary: Split data across multiple DB instances by a shard key. Enables horizontal scaling but complicates joins and transactions.

System Design.title: Message Queue
System Design.summary: Services communicate via messages rather than direct calls. Enables retries, rate limiting, and decoupling. Examples: Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis Pub/Sub.

System Design.title: CDN
System Design.summary: Cache static content at edge nodes close to users. Reduces origin server load and improves global latency significantly.

System Design.title: Rate Limiting
System Design.when: Abuse prevention, API quotas, fair usage
System Design.summary: Token bucket: smooth bursts. Leaky bucket: constant output rate. Sliding window: most accurate. Implement at the gateway, not inside services.

System Design.title: Consistent Hashing
System Design.when: Distributed caches, partitioning with dynamic node count
System Design.summary: Map nodes and keys to a ring. Adding/removing a node only remaps 1/n of keys instead of all of them. Virtual nodes improve balance.

System Design.title: SQL vs NoSQL
System Design.when: Every system design — justify your choice
System Design.summary: SQL: ACID, relations, structured schema. NoSQL: flexible schema, horizontal scale, eventual consistency. Pick based on query patterns, not hype.

System Design.title: Replication
System Design.summary: Leader–follower: writes go to leader, reads can go to replicas. Multi-leader: for geo-distributed writes. Leaderless (Dynamo style): highest availability.

System Design.title: CAP Theorem
System Design.summary: Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance — pick two. In practice, partitions happen, so choose CP (banks) or AP (social feeds) intentionally.

Behavioral.title: STAR Framework
Behavioral.summary: Situation → Task → Action → Result. Keep Situation and Task brief. Spend most time on Action (what YOU did) and Result (quantified impact).

Behavioral.title: Leadership Signals
Behavioral.when: "Tell me about a time you led..."
Behavioral.summary: Show initiative, influence without authority, and decision-making under ambiguity. Quantify team size and outcomes.

Behavioral.title: Conflict Resolution
Behavioral.summary: Show empathy, data-driven reasoning, and positive outcomes. Never blame. Focus on how you aligned toward a shared goal.

Behavioral.title: Failure Stories
Behavioral.summary: Own it fully. Show what you learned and what changed after. Interviewers want self-awareness and growth mindset.

Behavioral.title: Why This Company
Behavioral.summary: Be specific — reference their products, engineering culture, or recent launches. Generic answers are a red flag.

Behavioral.title: Ownership & Bias for Action
Behavioral.when: Amazon LP questions, any 'what did you do when blocked' prompt
Behavioral.summary: Show you acted without being told to. Quantify the unblocking. Distinguish between calculated risks you took and situations where you escalated correctly.

Behavioral.title: Ambiguity & Prioritization
Behavioral.summary: Show a framework: impact vs effort, stakeholder alignment, explicit trade-off communication. Avoid 'I just work harder' — that's not an answer.
